findings.title: Eager import() calls mean all apps load at import time and failed chunks become unhandled rejections
findings.body: The appStore object literal evaluates `import("./x")` for every app as soon as `@calcom/app-store` is first imported, so all ~29 app chunks start loading immediately on any code path that touches appStore — the intended deferral is not achieved for cold starts. Worse, each of these promises is created without a rejection handler: if any app chunk fails to load (a common case on Next.js/Vercel when in-flight requests reference chunks invalidated by a new deploy), the promise for that app rejects before anything awaits it. Since Node 15+, an unhandled rejection crashes the process by default, so one app's failed chunk can take down the whole server even though no request ever used that app. To be genuinely lazy and safe, the store should use getters (e.g. `get stripepayment() { return import("./stripepayment"); }`) so the import (and its promise) is only created when actually requested.

findings.title: async forEach discards deletion promises; reschedule completes before calendar/video events are deleted
findings.body: This PR changes `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach((bookingRef) => {...})` to `forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})`. `Array.forEach` ignores the returned promises, so nothing waits for the `getCalendar`/`deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` calls. Consequences: (1) `Reschedule` returns `true` and the reschedule email is sent before the external calendar events and video meetings are actually deleted; on a serverless platform the execution context can be frozen after the response, so the deletions may never run and stale events remain on users' calendars; (2) the surrounding `try/catch` cannot catch rejections from these async callbacks, so any failure becomes an unhandled promise rejection. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => ...))` instead.

findings.title: async forEach discards deletion promises; reschedule completes before calendar/video events are deleted
findings.body: This PR changes `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach((bookingRef) => {...})` to `forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})`. `Array.forEach` ignores the returned promises, so nothing waits for the `getCalendar`/`deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` calls. Consequences: (1) `Reschedule` returns `true` and the reschedule email is sent before the external calendar events and video meetings are actually deleted; on a serverless platform the execution context can be frozen after the response, so the deletions may never run and stale events remain on users' calendars; (2) the surrounding `try/catch` cannot catch rejections from these async callbacks, so any failure becomes an unhandled promise rejection. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => ...))` instead.

findings.title: requestReschedule fires-and-forgets calendar/video deletions via async forEach
findings.body: In the `requestReschedule` mutation, this PR changes `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach((bookingRef) => ...)` to `forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...)`. forEach does not await the async callbacks, so the mutation proceeds to send the reschedule-request email and webhooks and returns the response while the old calendar events (`calendar?.deleteEvent`) and video meetings (`deleteMeeting`) are still being — or have not yet begun to be — processed. There is also no try/catch or `.catch()` on these promises, so any deletion failure becomes an unhandled promise rejection. In a serverless environment the function can be suspended after the response, leaving the old calendar events permanently in place. Collect the promises with `.map()` and `await Promise.all(...)` before returning.

findings.title: Recurring-cancellation branch pushes into apiDeletes after awaits, racing the final Promise.all
findings.body: In the recurring-event cancellation branch (lines 458-470), the PR adds `await getCalendar(credential)` inside a `forEach(async (credential) => {...})` that pushes results into `apiDeletes`. Because forEach does not await the callbacks, the handler continues to line 652 (`await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))`) while the forEach callbacks are still suspended at their awaits; the Promise.all therefore snapshots a `apiDeletes` array that may be empty or partial, and the cancellation API response is returned before the calendar deletion calls have even been started. The attendee/bookingReference DB deletes then complete while external calendar events are still pending, so a subsequent process freeze or crash leaves external calendars with events that no longer exist in Cal.com. Convert the forEach to an awaited `Promise.all(credentials.map(...))` and push the deletion promises before awaiting them.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials creates getCalendar promises that are never awaited for non-calendar variants
findings.body: `getCalendarCredentials` now stores the un-awaited `getCalendar(credential)` promise in the returned objects, and only `getConnectedCalendars` awaits `item.calendar`. Two problems: (1) `getCalendar(credential)` is called for every app credential before the `app.variant === "calendar"` filter, so for non-calendar variants a promise is created and immediately discarded — if the app's dynamic import rejects, this is an unhandled rejection (fatal by default on Node 15+); (2) the exported return type of `getCalendarCredentials` silently changed from `calendar: Calendar | null` to `calendar: Promise<Calendar | null>`, a breaking contract change for any caller outside this file that accesses `.calendar` directly (they will now hold a Promise where they expect a service instance). Await the promise inside this function or only construct it for calendar-variant apps, and document/verify all callers.

findings.title: `await apiDeletes` awaits an array, not a promise, in the paid-booking branch
findings.body: In the paid-booking cancellation path, line 617 does `await apiDeletes;`. `apiDeletes` is an array of promises (populated by `deleteMeeting`/`calendar?.deleteEvent` calls which this PR makes asynchronous), not a promise itself, so awaiting it resolves immediately without waiting for any of the contained deletions. The comment says the code deliberately deletes booking references, but the external calendar/video deletions should still be awaited before returning, e.g. `await Promise.all(apiDeletes)`. Since this PR touches the surrounding async deletion logic, this is the place to fix it.

findings.title: No tests accompany the async conversion of booking create/cancel/reschedule flows
findings.body: This PR changes the timing semantics of core booking flows: getCalendar/getVideoAdappers/deleteMeeting became async, appStore lookups are now awaited dynamic imports, and several loops became async forEach. None of these paths (calendar event creation/update/deletion, booking cancellation, reschedule request, payment refund) have accompanying tests added or updated in the PR. Given the fire-and-forget issues this conversion introduces (deletion promises not awaited), at minimum regression tests for cancel/reschedule asserting that external deletions are awaited before the handler resolves should be added before merging.
